claim: RAT-SQL does name-based schema linking by string-matching question n-grams (length 1-5) against column/table names as exact/partial(subsequence)/no match, encoding these as directional relation labels that bias a relation-aware self-attention encoder.
quote: for all n-grams of length 1 to 5 in the question, we determine (1) whether it exactly matches the name of a column/table (exact match); or (2) whether the n-gram is a subsequence of the name ... M is one of ExactMatch, PartialMatch, or NoMatch.

claim: Schema linking aligns NL questions with schema elements; using the full schema adds irrelevant context, token overhead and hallucinations that cut accuracy, and prior methods show a recall/false-positive tradeoff (CHESS 97.12% recall / 30.57% FPR; RSL-SQL 93.28% recall / 68.23% FPR), which a bidirectional table-first + column-first union approach tries to balance.
quote: Schema linking---the process of aligning natural language questions with database schema elements ... Using the full schema introduces irrelevant context, increases token overhead, and often leads to hallucinations ... CHESS achieves the highest recall (97.12%) but at the cost of an elevated false positive rate (30.57%) ... RSL-SQL reports strong recall (93.28%) yet suffers from a high FPR (68.23%)

claim: CRUSH4SQL instructs an LLM to hallucinate a minimal schema for a query, then uses collective dense retrieval against the real schema, achieving higher recall than prior retrieval methods on large databases (up to 17,844 schema elements).
quote: instruct[s] an LLM to hallucinate a minimal DB schema deemed adequate to answer the query ... leads to significantly higher recall than SOTA retrieval-based augmentation methods

claim: A 2024 survey groups schema linking into three eras (string-matching/similarity, neural-network alignment, LLM in-context-learning), notes it identifies the relevant tables/columns and is essential for accuracy, and is even more critical in the LLM era due to input-length limits.
quote: Early research primarily focused on string matching techniques ... researchers have employed deep neural networks ... leverage their strong reasoning capabilities for schema linking ... This step is essential for improving the performance of the Text-to-SQL task ... In the LLM era, schema linking has become even more critical due to the input length limitations of LLMs.

claim: CHESS retrieves schema-relevant values via model-generated keywords, locality-sensitive hashing for ANN value search and a vector DB for semantic catalog search, then applies adaptive schema pruning (column filter, table select, final column select); ablation shows giving the LLM all information confuses it, so selective retrieval is crucial.
quote: LSH is an effective technique for approximate nearest-neighbor searches ... preprocesses database catalogs into a vector database ... providing an LLM with all available information can confuse the model and selective retrieval is crucial for achieving higher performance.

claim: DAIL-SQL evaluated five question representations (Basic, Text Representation, OpenAI Demonstration, Code Representation, Alpaca SFT) across four LLMs in zero-shot, finding Code Representation and OpenAI Demonstration prompts preferred.
quote: Code Representation Prompt and OpenAI Demonstration Prompt are preferred

claim: DAIL-SQL with GPT-4 reaches 83.5% execution accuracy on Spider-dev and 86.6% on the Spider leaderboard using code-style schema representation plus selected demonstrations.
quote: DAIL-SQL equipped with GPT-4 achieves an execution accuracy of 83.5% on Spider-dev ... achieved 86.6% execution accuracy on the Spider leaderboard

claim: Alibaba's XiYan-SQL introduces M-Schema, a semi-structured representation using special tokens for the database, tables and foreign keys, encoding each column as a tuple of name, data type, description, primary-key flag, and example values.
quote: M-Schema ... employs specifical tokens for identification ... marks the database, # Table signifies tables, and ... indicates foreign keys

claim: M-Schema, derived from MAC-SQL schema, is a more compact representation that adds explicit data types, primary-key markings, richer column descriptions pulled from the database, and revised sample-value display rules.
quote: Derived from MAC-SQL Schema, M-Schema is a more compact representation that adds data types, primary key markings, and changes the rules for displaying sample values

claim: BIRD's oracle external-knowledge/evidence field lifts dev-set EX (ChatGPT 37.22%→42.24%, GPT-4 46.35%→49.15%); the test-set leaderboard tops out at AskData+GPT-4o 81.95%, Agentar-Scale-SQL 81.67%, Xiaomi Text2SQL 80.83%, LongData-SQL 77.53%, SiriusAI 77.03%, vs a 92.96% human baseline.
quote: AskData + GPT-4o 81.95%; Agentar-Scale-SQL 81.67%; Xiaomi Text2SQL 80.83%; LongData-SQL 77.53%; SiriusAI-Text2SQL-Agent 77.03%; Human Performance 92.96%. ChatGPT 37.22% dev without evidence → 42.24% with evidence; GPT-4 46.35% → 49.15%

claim: BIRD's external knowledge spans four sources (numeric reasoning, domain knowledge, synonym, value illustration); the ~20-point swing from adding evidence is reproducible, but hand-written per-query evidence is unrealistic since a deployed agent must retrieve domain context itself.
quote: the external knowledge evidence is hand-written, per-query, by annotators with domain expertise, which is not a realistic deployment scenario—a real NL-to-SQL agent must retrieve or infer the relevant domain context itself

claim: RSL-SQL injects a few randomly selected sample rows per table so the LLM can understand the potential values and semantics of each column, truncating overly long values to keep input manageable.
quote: Randomly selected a few rows from each table, allowing LLMs to gain a better understanding of the potential values of each column and semantics of the tables and columns.

claim: Spider 2.0 enterprise databases often exceed 1,000 columns (some over 3,000), and naive LLMs collapse: o1-preview solves only 17.1% and GPT-4o only 10.1% of tasks, versus 86.6% for GPT-4o on Spider 1.0; the Spider 2.0-Lite leaderboard now tops out at DivSkill-SQL 73.13%.
quote: o1-preview solve only 17.1% of Spider 2.0 tasks ... GPT-4o, the success rate is only 10.1% on Spider 2.0 tasks, compared to 86.6% on Spider 1.0. Spider 2.0-Lite top performer: DivSkill-SQL 73.13%

claim: LinkAlign frames schema linking on large multi-database settings as a coarse-to-fine pipeline: multi-round semantic retrieval with query rewriting to find candidate schemas, argmax LLM selection of the target database, then multi-agent debate to extract tables/columns; it reaches 33.09% execution accuracy on Spider 2.0-Lite with open-source LLMs.
quote: Achieves 33.09% execution accuracy on Spider 2.0-Lite benchmark using open-source LLMs—state-of-the-art at submission time.

claim: CRED-SQL's CLSR clusters columns by semantic similarity with K-means and weights rare attributes higher (inverse cluster size), boosting large-DB table recall to 0.40@1 / 0.77@3 on SpiderUnion versus CRUSH's 0.09@1, and lifting end-to-end accuracy to 73.4% (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B), ~22 points over CRUSH.
quote: CLSR achieves 0.40 recall @1 vs. CRUSH's 0.09 ... SpiderUnion: CRED-SQL achieves 73.4% with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B ... Outperforms CRUSH by ~22 percentage points on SpiderUnion

claim: LitE-SQL pre-computes per-column embeddings (column name, description, table name, value description, types, keys, sample values) with a fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B-Embedding model, stores them in ChromaDB, and at inference retrieves top-k=25 columns by cosine similarity, cutting latency to ~25s vs CHESS's ~84s while hitting 72.1% EX on BIRD.
quote: pre-computes schema embeddings ... stored in ChromaDB ... The optimal k-value is empirically set to 25 ... LitE-SQL: 24.979 seconds average inference latency ... CHESS (200B): 83.631 seconds

claim: Schema pruning helps even when models could fit the full schema: with oracle schema, pruning 71.3% of columns raised execution accuracy from 79.3% to 86.3%; small models with <2k-token context windows cannot fit large schemas, motivating splitting schemas into parallel chunks of up to 64 columns, with literal values found by keyword-matching question terms to cell values (top-3 per column).
quote: smaller models usually have shorter context windows (i.e. <2k tokens) ... Full schema: 79.3% ... Pruned schema (71.3% reduction): 86.3% accuracy ... we select values for columns ... by simply matching keywords in questions and values

claim: Fixed top-k retrieval over schema is brittle because too-small k drops needed tables and too-large k injects noise; a RAG architecture with hierarchical clustering can dynamically determine how many relevant schemas to return instead of a static k.
quote: introducing a unique hierarchical clustering mechanism to dynamically determine the number of relevant schemas, minimizing noise ... fixing k can lead to errors where irrelevant tables are included as noise or necessary tables are missing

claim: PICARD constrains autoregressive decoding via incremental parsing, rejecting inadmissible tokens at each step to find valid SQL output sequences.
quote: PICARD helps to find valid output sequences by rejecting inadmissible tokens at each decoding step. ... checking, accepting, and rejecting of tokens and token sequences is achieved through parsing

claim: PICARD lifts T5-3B on Spider dev from 71.5% to 75.5% exact-set match and from 74.4% to 79.3% execution accuracy, reaching 75.1% execution accuracy on test.
quote: Development Set: Exact-set Match Accuracy 75.5%, Execution Accuracy 79.3%. Test Set: ... Execution Accuracy 75.1%. ... without PICARD ... 71.5% exact-set match and 74.4% execution accuracy

claim: DIN-SQL adds a human-written self-correction module that revises initially generated SQL, achieving 85.3 execution accuracy on the Spider test set.
quote: DIN-SQL designs a human-written self-correction guideline and revises all the initially generated SQLs according to this guideline ... achieving execution accuracy of 85.3 on the Spider test set

claim: On Spider dev, DIN-SQL self-correction adds ~1.73 points (78.62% to 80.35%), while MAGIC's auto-generated guideline from failure analysis reaches 85.66% execution accuracy.
quote: DIN-SQL achieves 78.62% execution accuracy on Spider's development set without self-correction. With self-correction ... 80.35% ... MAGIC achieves 85.66% execution accuracy on Spider

claim: MAC-SQL's Refiner executes candidate SQL, captures execution-error feedback, and re-prompts to repair queries, helping reach 59.59% on BIRD test and 86.75% on Spider dev.
quote: the Refiner (for validating and refining defective SQL queries) ... employs an external tool for SQL execution, obtains feedback, and refines erroneous SQL ... 59.59% on the BIRD test set and 86.75% on the Spider development set

claim: CSC-SQL merges self-consistency and self-correction by feeding the two most frequent sampled SQLs into a merge-revision model, reaching 73.67% on BIRD private test (32B).
quote: CSC selects the two most frequently occurring outputs from parallel sampling and feeds them into a merge revision model for correction ... BIRD Private Test Set: 32B model 73.67% execution accuracy

claim: Execution-guided decoding excludes faulty partial programs by conditioning on partial execution, reaching 83.8% execution accuracy on WikiSQL.
quote: Execution guidance ... detecting and excluding faulty programs during the decoding procedure by conditioning on the execution of partially generated program ... state-of-the-art execution accuracy of 83.8% on WikiSQL

claim: A 2026 single-agent self-refinement + ensemble (weighted majority) voting pipeline (SSEV) reaches 85.5%/86.4% on Spider dev/test and 66.3% on BIRD-dev without ground-truth data.
quote: Single-Agent Self-Refinement with Ensemble Voting (SSEV) ... Spider 1.0-Dev: 85.5% ... Spider 1.0-Test: 86.4% ... BIRD-Dev: 66.3% ... integrates Weighted Majority Voting (WMV) and its randomized variant

claim: XiYan-SQL reaches 75.63% EX on BIRD test and 89.65% on Spider test; its ablation shows schema linking adds about 2.15 points (57.95% to 60.10%) and the M-Schema representation beats DDL schema by an average 2.03% across four LLMs.
quote: M-Schema demonstrated superior performance compared to DDL Schema, with an average increase of 2.03%; schema linking improved execution accuracy by 2.15 percentage points (57.95% to 60.10%)

claim: CHASE-SQL achieves 73.01% dev / 73.0% test EX on BIRD; ablations show divide-and-conquer CoT contributes -1.24% when removed, query-plan CoT -0.65%, synthetic examples -0.85%, the fine-tuned selection agent beats self-consistency by ~4-5 points, and the oracle upper bound with perfect candidate selection is 82.79%.
quote: With perfect selection from all three generators combined: 82.79% execution accuracy; Without Divide-and-Conquer CoT: -1.24%; Without Query Plan CoT: -0.65%; Without Online Synthetic Examples: -0.85%

claim: The 'Death of Schema Linking?' paper finds that with strong reasoning models full-schema prompting reaches 94.62% EX and explicit schema-linking filters cause net losses (e.g. table-to-column linking drops to as low as 9.79%); top models like Gemini 1.5 Pro see a net EX reduction when schema linking is applied, while weaker models still benefit from filtering.
quote: Top performing models, such as Gemini 1.5 Pro, see a net reduction in EX when schema linking is applied, while weaker models still benefit from filtering approaches; Full Schema: 94.62% execution accuracy

claim: Snowflake's Arctic-Text2SQL-R1, a smaller RL-trained model, tops BIRD and wins broadly, showing reinforcement-learning post-training competing with large ensemble pipelines on schema-grounded SQL generation.
quote: Smaller Models, Smarter SQL: Arctic-Text2SQL-R1 Tops BIRD and Wins Broadly

claim: Vanna grounds text-to-SQL via a RAG model trained on DDL, documentation, and example SQL queries, retrieving the most relevant training items into the prompt at query time.
quote: train a RAG "model" on your data, and then ask questions which will return SQL queries

claim: Vanna's training accepts DDL statements (vn.train(ddl=...)), business documentation, and SQL queries, and retrieves the 10 most relevant training pieces per question to build the LLM prompt.
quote: Vanna will retrieve 10 most relevant pieces of training data and use it as part of the LLM prompt to generate the SQL.

claim: WrenAI is an open context layer (15.5k+ GitHub stars) that encodes schema, metrics, and relationships into Modeling Definition Language (MDL) to give LLM agents grounded, governed SQL across 20+ data sources.
quote: open context layer that gives AI agents grounded, governed memory, context, SQL across 20+ data sources

claim: Wren AI's MDL defines entities mapped to tables/columns, metrics, dimensions, filters and transformations so business meaning (e.g. 'total sales') is defined once and reused rather than re-inferred per query.
quote: the meaning of 'total sales'... is defined once and reused

claim: Dataherald (3.6k stars) is an agentic text-to-SQL engine that grounds via schema tools, a Context Store of business/data logic, and a GetFewShotExamples tool that dynamically retrieves golden Question/SQL pairs.
quote: GetFewShotExamples tool... allowing the agent to request relevant Question/SQL pairs dynamically

claim: LlamaIndex NLSQLTableQueryEngine injects table schema context into the prompt; for many tables it uses SQLTableNodeMapping to index per-table schemas (ObjectIndex) and retrieve only relevant tables to avoid context overflow.
quote: if the total size of table schemas overflows your context window, you can store the table schema in an index using the SQLTableNodeMapping object

claim: LlamaIndex (50k+ stars) provides NLSQLRetriever and NLSQLQueryEngine components that retrieve table schemas plus sample rows to improve SQL generation accuracy.
quote: NLSQLRetriever and NLSQLQueryEngine components, retrieving table schemas, contextual structure overviews, and actual data rows

claim: LangChain (138k+ stars) provides SQLDatabase/SQLDatabaseChain utilities but requires careful prompt engineering and schema filtering for large databases.
quote: LangChain excels at building production-ready applications but requires careful prompt engineering and schema filtering for large databases

claim: Snowflake Cortex Analyst grounds text-to-SQL on a YAML semantic model defining logical tables, dimensions, facts, metrics, relationships, synonyms, and verified queries, because raw schemas lack business definitions and metric handling.
quote: Generic AI solutions often struggle with text-to-SQL conversions when given only a database schema, as schemas lack critical knowledge like business process definitions and metrics handling.

claim: Databricks Genie grounds on Unity Catalog metadata (table/column descriptions, RLS policies), while BigQuery Gemini reads Dataform-defined views plus Information Schema; Cortex Analyst ships its own YAML semantic model.
quote: Reads metadata from Unity Catalog (table descriptions, column comments, row-level security policies)

claim: The dbt Semantic Layer reports 83% NL-query accuracy when grounding text-to-SQL on its metrics/dimensions/entities ontology versus ~40% for LLMs writing raw SQL against undecorated tables.
quote: 83% accuracy on natural language queries when backed by the semantic layer, compared to approximately 40% accuracy when LLMs write raw SQL against undecorated tables

claim: The Open Semantic Interchange (OSI), released January 2026, is a vendor-neutral YAML standard for semantic metadata backed by Snowflake, dbt Labs, Cube, Databricks, AtScale and 40+ partners, aimed at portable LLM grounding.
quote: Open Semantic Interchange specification, released in January 2026, is a vendor-neutral, YAML-based standard for representing semantic metadata
